rows: Windows broken throughout Robert Lee due to hail.
Thunderstorm winds knocked down trees near Robert Lee.
Along with the 70 mph winds, nickel size hail was also reported on highway 158 west of Robert Lee.
Quarter size hail reported in Robert Lee.
This is a continuation of the tornado that developed in northern Tom Green county. The tornado dissipated near the community of Tennyson and remained in open country with only damage to trees.
Law Enforcement Officials witnessed a tornado for several minutes. No damage was noted as the tornado remained in open fields.
Hail lasted for several minutes. Damage to roofs and cars was observed.
A Game Warden reported golf ball size hail.
Large hail damaged homes and vehicles.
Power lines were blown down just north of Bronte.
A trained storm spotter reporter nickel size hail with lots of dime size hail covering State Highway 158.
Large hail lasted for approximately five minutes followed by a downpour of smaller hail.
A trained spotter relayed a report of nickel to quarter size hail along State Highway 158 just west of Lake E.V. Spence.
A wind gust of 60 mph was reported.
A National Weather Service Cooperative Observer estimated a 75 mph wind gust.
The fire department reported residential roofs were damaged by the strong winds.
The public estimated a wind gust to 60 mph 5 miles northwest of Tennyson.

An observer had witnessed the tornado touching the ground multiple times about 4 miles southwest of Silver. This tornado path length and beginning time were estimated using radar data and eyewitness accounts. The path width was also estimated.
